## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f5ff7bf0a675f84734aa0b7158210cb9929b0bb`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #11211 (body and its three comments: triage `5911720106`, claim `5927341597`, dev report `5927597493`); PR #11359 (body, three-file list, net diff `2124d04111..6f5ff7bf0a`: one commit, +177/−40); the 42 check-runs on the head. The merge-base of the head and `origin/main` is `2124d04111`, the claim's BASE.

**(a) The href change — right.** `MobileBottomNav` now reads `const { href, external } = resolveHref(item, basePath)` for every leaf. `basePath` is the `AppSchemaRenderer` prop that `InternalSidebar` hands `NavigationRenderer` (`basePath={basePath}`), and neither side passes a template context: `InternalSidebar`'s `NavigationRenderer` call carries no `templateContext`, and `AppSchemaRendererProps` has no such prop (the word occurs in the file only in the new comment). So the bar's call is `resolveHref(item, basePath, undefined)`, the sidebar's exact arguments; nothing invented. The seven hand-rolled branches (`object` with `viewName`, `dashboard`, `page`, `report`, `url`, `component` with its own `URLSearchParams` loop, and the `doc` delegation) are deleted in one hunk; at the head `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx` holds no `${basePath}` template at all, so no second copy of the href rule exists. `resolveHref` and `NavigationRenderer.tsx` are untouched.

**(b) Deviation (a), the highlight — forced and in scope.** The bar now reads `resolveActiveNavItem(items, location.pathname, location.search, basePath)?.id ?? null` and lights the tab whose `item.id` equals it. That is the sidebar's own election, called the same way: `NavigationRenderer` computes `resolveActiveNavItem(items, location.pathname, location.search, basePath, templateContext)` once at the tree root, with `templateContext` undefined inside `AppSchemaRenderer`, over the same `items` (`resolvedNavigation`). Forced: the ruled change makes the `filters` and `runAction` hrefs carry a query string, and the old `location.pathname.startsWith(href)` can never match one, so the ruled change alone darkens those tabs on their own page; ablation C measured exactly that (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Open Tasks' ]`). The `resolveActiveNavItem` docblock requires every "which menu am I in" surface to use it. Not a widening: no new rule, no new argument; the bar consumes the inverse of the call the direction names. One consequence noted, not escalated: the election runs over the whole tree while the bar draws five leaves, so when the sidebar's elected row is a sixth-or-later leaf no tab lights. That is the sidebar's answer rendered faithfully, which is the card's measure.

**(c) Deviation (b), the external anchor — in scope as a bounded in-place fix.** `resolveHref` returns one answer, `{ href, external }`; at the base the bar consumed `.href` and dropped `external`, so a `url` entry with `target: '_blank'` opened in the app's own window where the sidebar opens a new tab. The head draws such a tab as a plain anchor with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, the sidebar's own markup (the `NavigationRenderer` leaf branch). This is the deviation closest to the line, since the card's measured defect is "a different page" and here the page matched; it is accepted because it is the same call's second field on the very `url` branch the direction deletes, and leaving it would keep the bar diverging from the sidebar on an entry type this fix touches. Same function, same test family, one pin and one ablation. Not a widening: no prop, no new rule, nothing for the out-of-scope card.

**(d) Pins — sound.** The committed file `packages/layout/src/__tests__/AppSchemaRenderer.mobileTabHref-11211.test.tsx` holds seven tests: five rows (the plain `object` control plus the card's four) and two for the in-place fixes. Each row asserts three equalities: `resolveHref`'s answer equals the card's table (so the row exercises the branch it names), the tab's `href` equals `resolveHref`'s answer, and the tab's `href` equals the sidebar link the same entry draws in the same render. The third is the card's measure itself; it catches a wrong `basePath`, an invented template context, or a re-spelled branch that diverges on any row. Red first at `2124d04111`: 6 failed, 1 passed, with the card's exact tab hrefs as the Received values and the control green, as it should be (both spellings agreed on it). Ablations A–D on the committed fix each redden exactly their rows (A: record, filters, runAction; B: metadata; C: active; D: external), and restore was proven by blob hash `877264451d4b`, which is the head's blob for the file in the diff header. The dev's "9 passed (9)" counts a scratch probe deleted before commit; the committed file is 7 and every ablation leg reports 7. Package suite 321/321 is the dev's local figure; the CI shards that run it are not concluded (see (g)).

**Accept-set and public surface:** none changes. `AppSchemaRendererProps`, `packages/layout/src/index.ts` (the `app-schema-renderer` node and its `mobileNavMode` enum input) and `NavigationRenderer.tsx` are untouched; the one import added is `resolveActiveNavItem`, already exported. The bar's rendered DOM changes within the published component (an external tab is a plain anchor with `target` and `rel`; the lit tab follows the election), which the changeset states.

**(g) CI on the head.** 42 check-runs, read once at record time: 30 completed success, 3 skipped (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, the coverage shard), 9 in_progress and NOT concluded: `Type Check`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Test (shard 1/8)`, `2/8`, `3/8`, `4/8`, `6/8`, `7/8`, `8/8`. Those are the runs that execute the new pin and `tsc` on the head; nothing has failed. This record does not treat them as pass; the seat sees them conclude before merge.

### ② Semver level

One changeset `.changeset/11211-layout-mobile-tab-resolvehref.md`: `@object-ui/layout` `patch`. Right: a bug fix inside a published component, no API change. Its text is true against the diff: the four card rows; `page` entries dropping `params` and `recordMode: 'edit'` ignored (both true of the deleted branches, since the old `page` branch wrote `${basePath}/page/${pageName}` only and the old `object` branch read neither `recordId` nor `recordMode`); and the two following behaviours (one lit tab, the sidebar's; `target: '_blank'` opens a new tab). No `skip-changeset` label; Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Claim Re-read, Fixed Group Check and Overwrite Report all concluded success.

`Clause-②: no` — right. No prop, export, type or accepted value changes; the bar converges on the published `resolveHref` / `resolveActiveNavItem` pair. The PR body carries the same line.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

Deviations, each answered:
1. Scope (a) and (b): answered in ① (b) and (c). Accepted as the bounded exemption; both are declared in the PR body with ablation evidence, and no other claim holds the file.
2. Pins beyond the ruled five: the active-state pin and the external pin. Accepted; each pins one in-place fix and has its own ablation leg.
3. Commit trailer: the head commit ends with the model-free pair (`Claude-Session` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`), as objectui AGENTS.md requires (its rule quotes the objectstack ruling verbatim and says the harness precedence rule enforces it). Accepted, nothing to escalate. No model identifier in the PR title, body, changeset, pin or code comment.
4. Ablation tool: objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` run with cwd in the objectui worktree. Accepted; the restore proof names the objectui head blob.

Out-of-scope findings — two cards, not one:
1. **Fileable, class a, one card.** Reach measured at the published export `AppSchemaRenderer` / SDUI node `app-schema-renderer` with `mobileNavMode: 'bottom_nav'`, at both `2124d04111` and `6f5ff7bf0a`. Consistent with the head: `MobileBottomNav` receives `resolvedNavigation` unguarded and `collectLeaves` applies none of the sidebar's `passesNavItemGuards` (`visible`, `requiredPermissions`, capability, doc target, `hasActionHandler`), so a hidden or permission-denied entry is drawn as a tab and an `action` entry as a dead link. One site, one fix (run the leaves through the sidebar's `guardOptions`), one pin family, so one card for all three symptoms. A different class from this card's href rule, and triage's direction named hrefs only, so leaving it unfixed here was right. Dedupe words as the dev gave them.
2. **Fileable, class c, its own card.** Named producer: `skills/objectui/guides/mobile.md` lines 75–77 teach setting `mobileNavMode` on the app schema that `AppSchemaRenderer` renders. The head reads `mobileNavMode` only as a prop (`AppSchemaRenderer.tsx` lines 91, 517, 629) and declares it only as the node input (`index.ts` line 286), never from `schema`; the dev measured objectui's `AppComponentSchema` keeping the key. Separate site, class and fix surface (governed `skills/**`, own PR) from finding 1, so a second card. The filer records as NOT measured whether objectstack's strict spec refuses the key, and leaves to triage whether the fix is the guide's wording or a renderer read of the document key.

**VERDICT: PASS**
